subject: Order form: forecasting, billing lag, and tax allocation
messages:
From: Nathan Lee <nathan.lee@nimblepay.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@nimblepay.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 16:24:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions — billing cadence, minimum commits, tax responsibility

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to internal approval but a few commercial items remain blocking Procurement and Finance: can you help confirm the specifics below so we can circulate a final PO?

Quick list of asks:
- Billing cadence and expected billing lag (we need to budget for invoice timing vs consumption). If usage-based, invoicing period and when it's due.
- Treatment of over/under usage against a minimum commit: proration examples and whether credits or invoice adjustments apply.
- Tax/VAT responsibility: for EU customers we need to confirm whether Redwood will collect VAT or if NimblePay must self-account.
- Net payment terms — we typically require Net 45 for startups; curious if Net 30 is possible or if you can offer a short-term credit arrangement.
- PO and remittance fields: required line items and whether Redwood can accept our standard PO number on the invoice.

If helpful, Procurement is available for a 30-min call Thursday morning. Appreciate a short written reply we can attach to our internal approval packet.

Thanks,
Nathan Lee
Procurement Manager
NimblePay, Inc.
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
To: Nathan Lee <nathan.lee@nimblepay.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 18:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — billing cadence, minimum commits, tax responsibility

Nathan — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (sales) and Kimberly (finance) to confirm policy and propose language we can include in the Order Form. I've attached a redline (Order_Form_Redlines_v2.docx) with inline suggestions — high level answers below, and we can adjust on the call.

Proposed (high level):
- Billing cadence: monthly in arrears for consumption-based usage. Invoices issued within 5 business days after period close; standard processing time is 7–10 business days (i.e., you should expect to see a charge on the invoice for the prior month).
- Billing lag: example — August usage appears on invoice issued Sep 5 and payable per net terms from that invoice date.
- Minimum commit proration: if a committed monthly minimum is defined, overage is billed monthly at the agreed unit price; under-utilization is handled per the Order Form: either (a) non-refundable monthly minimum charges, or (b) true-up at quarter end if you prefer smoothing — see redline options A/B.
- Tax/VAT: by default, customer is responsible for VAT and similar indirect taxes. We can add language to gross-up if Redwood is required to collect VAT in a jurisdiction; Kimberly can confirm the exact phrasing.
- Net terms: Redwood standard is Net 30 for enterprise agreements; for new customers we can accept Net 45 with a short-term arrangement or a 10% prepayment / deposit against the first invoice. Ben — can you confirm commercial flexibility?

Next steps:
1) Ben to propose a Net term / deposit tradeoff.
2) Kimberly to provide definitive tax clause language.
3) Nathan / Procurement to confirm whether they want quarterly true-up or monthly non-refundable minimum.

Happy to join the Thursday slot if that helps.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Nathan Lee <nathan.lee@nimblepay.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — billing cadence, minimum commits, tax responsibility

Nathan — quick commercial proposal from my side to get Procurement moving:

Option 1 (standard): Net 30, monthly invoices in arrears, customer responsible for VAT. Minimum commit billed monthly (non-refundable).

Option 2 (expedited approval): Net 45 for first 6 months + 10% advance credit applied to the first invoice. After 6 months, revert to Net 30 if usage and payment history meet our credit guidelines.

Example proration language (for Order Form):
- If Customer commits to X units/month and uses Y < X, Customer is charged for X at the agreed rate for that month unless parties elect quarterly true-up, in which case underutilization may be credited against future periods up to the committed amount for the quarter.

If NimblePay prefers simplicity for accounting, Option 2 tends to unblock internal approval quickly (adds a small deposit so finance feels covered). I can markup the Order Form with whichever option you prefer.

Tessa — happy to join the call Thursday AM.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
To: Nathan Lee <nathan.lee@nimblepay.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 11:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — billing cadence, minimum commits, tax responsibility

Nathan — a few precise items Finance needs for the Order Form and invoice processing: 

1) Tax/VAT: Redwood will by default state that Customer is responsible for any VAT, GST, or similar taxes on top of the fees. If local law requires Redwood to collect VAT, we will collect and remit; we will provide the VAT registration number and an invoice showing the VAT amount. Wording we propose: "Customer shall be responsible for all sales, use, value-added and similar taxes (excluding taxes based on Redwood's net income). If Redwood is required to collect or remit VAT in Customer's jurisdiction, Redwood will charge and remit such VAT and provide tax documentation on the invoice."

2) PO number: we can accept a Customer PO number as a reference on the invoice; please confirm the exact PO string to ensure matching. 

3) Invoice cadence: monthly in arrears, invoice issued within 5 business days following the month end. Payment due per Net terms from invoice date.

4) Prepayment: if the customer prefers Net 45, Finance requests a 10% advance deposit applied to the first invoice OR a short-term credit check (we rarely make exceptions without either).

Attached is an invoice sample (Invoice_Sample_2027Q3.pdf) that shows the fields we populate — if you can confirm the remittance address and PO field we should be good.

Let me know if Procurement needs specific invoicing language for their internal controls; we can include a short clause in the Order Form.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Nathan Lee <nathan.lee@nimblepay.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@nimblepay.ai, ben.carter@redwood.inference, kimberly.park@redwood.inference
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — billing cadence, minimum commits, tax responsibility

Tessa / team — thanks, that is very helpful and should resolve most internal questions. A few follow-ups: 

- Procurement prefers quarterly true-up versus non-refundable monthly minimums for cashflow reasons; please include Option A (quarterly true-up) as the default with an override to select non-refundable monthly minimum if we explicitly tick that box.
- We'll accept Option 2 (Net 45 + 10% deposit) to speed approval; can you send the Order Form clean with that option pre-selected and signature blocks for both parties?
- Please include the VAT clause Kimberly suggested and the sample invoice fields in the Order Form appendix.

If you can get the clean Order Form (Order_Form_Clean_v3.pdf) back to us by end of day Friday, Procurement will try to route the PO next week. We can do a short signature/DocuSign afterward.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Nathan Lee
Procurement Manager
NimblePay, Inc.
